fact: The first literal computer 'bug' was a moth taped into the Harvard Mark II logbook in 1947, labelled 'first actual case of bug being found'.
In 2011, researchers took down web servers in many languages by posting form fields whose keys all hashed to the same bucket. That's why .NET now randomizes string hash codes per process.
Tony Hoare called inventing the null reference in 1965 his 'billion-dollar mistake'. C#'s nullable reference types are a decades-later fix.
A TCP handshake is SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. With TLS 1.3 on top, the first HTTP request goes out after just 2 round trips. HTTP/3 over QUIC can do it in 1.
Linus Torvalds wrote the first version of Git in about two weeks in 2005, after the Linux kernel lost free access to BitKeeper.
MongoDB documents are capped at 16 MB. If you're near that, your model is telling you to reference instead of embed.
Kubernetes is Greek for 'helmsman' or 'pilot'. The 7 spokes on its logo nod to its Google codename, Project Seven of Nine.
Brendan Eich created the first version of JavaScript in about 10 days in 1995. Some of its quirks (typeof null === 'object') date from then.
The leap second on 30 June 2012 sent many Linux servers into CPU spins through a kernel timer bug, hitting sites like Reddit and LinkedIn.
xkcd's 'Little Bobby Tables' (Robert'); DROP TABLE Students;--) is still the best one-line explanation of why you parameterize queries.
